caption: A candle burns on a dinner table, and melted wax spills over the rim and runs down one side.

sa.check: A lit candle stands on a table.
A pool of melted wax sits at the candle's top.
The wax runs down one side of the candle.
The pool lies around the flame at the candle's top.
The order is pool, spill over the rim, run down.

pc.expect: The overflow runs downward along the candle's side from the rim where it spilled.
pc.fail: Wax runs up the candle's side; or climbs back over the rim into the pool; or a run travels sideways round the candle and stays level; or a drop leaves the candle and floats.

pc.expect: The run only advances down the side and stops where it has cooled, and what has set stays set.
pc.fail: A set run high on the candle turns liquid again with no fresh wax reaching it; or the run retreats up the candle; or the candle grows taller as the wax runs; or the run advances and withdraws in turn.

pc.expect: The wax is a thin liquid in the pool near the flame and a dull raised ridge where it has run and cooled.
pc.fail: A run stays glossy and runny far below wax that has already set dull above it; or a run sets as a spike standing out sideways from the candle; or the candle's body sags or bends as a whole; or the pool sets into a hard skin while the flame burns in it.

pc.expect: The pool sits at the top around the flame and the spill starts at its rim.
pc.fail: Wax spills over the rim while the candle's top is dry and solid; or the pool lies away from the flame while the wax beside the flame stays solid; or a run appears part-way down the candle with no wax coming over the rim above it.

pc.expect: One candle with one wick and one flame; wax moves from pool to side to table.
pc.fail: The candle grows taller; or a second candle or flame appears; or the flame detaches from the wick and floats; or wax appears on the table with no run reaching it.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The candle's colour, the holder and the table stay the same.
pc.fail: The candle changes colour; or the table's pattern changes; or the holder moves or vanishes.
